content.text:
Sono **tre** Location, non due: ho dovuto aggiungere **Seven Hills**.

Il motivo: nella tua gerarchia Villa Douglas è marcata `[I]` Internal dentro Seven Hills, e in Wyvern questo si rende col campo Parent Location. Ma il genitore deve esistere prima, altrimenti il menu a tendina è vuoto e Villa Douglas resterebbe appesa direttamente a Blackwood City perdendo l'ereditarietà. Seven Hills era già scritta in `locations.md`, quindi è copia e incolla.

**Perché queste due sono un ottimo test**

Lunar Quad e Villa Douglas sono i poli opposti del mondo: campus pubblico, affollato e libero contro casa privata, sorvegliata e soffocante. Se in chat le due atmosfere risultano nettamente diverse, sai che il sistema Environment→Location→Final Instructions sta funzionando davvero.

E su Villa Douglas testi anche la catena completa a quattro livelli: World Formatting Rules → Blackwood City → Seven Hills → Villa Douglas, con le istruzioni più specifiche che vincono.

**Cosa ho arricchito**

`locations.md` per Villa Douglas era essenzialmente vuoto. Ho preso la Sensory Signature da `Master_Design.md` (Standing Location 1): il cuoio tattico, il cedro, il sentore di carne cruda, la ventilazione che isola l'aggressività, le porte oversize per gli Hybrid Shift, la Pack Bathhouse. Sono i dettagli che dicono all'AI che questa non è una villa di lusso qualsiasi ma la tana di un branco.

Ho anche messo l'indirizzo canonico 555 Oak Road dalle trigger keywords.

Fermati un attimo — c'è un problema che invalida i numeri delle Era.

**Il form dice: `World Start Time: Monday, January 1, Year 2024 CE`**

Ma noi abbiamo impostato il Timeline Start a **1 gennaio 800**. Il sistema sta ancora leggendo l'anno **2024** come hour 0.

È esattamente il rischio che avevo segnalato quando hai detto di aver lasciato il calendario gregoriano di default: lo **Start Year del Calendar** è un campo separato dal Timeline Start Date, ed è rimasto a 2024.

Conseguenza pratica: tutte le ore delle Era sono sbagliate. Con hour 0 = 2024, il valore `9712500` che ho dato per la fondazione della SUCC non punta al 1908, punta all'anno **3132 circa**. Stessa cosa per Age of Secrecy e tutte le altre.

**Vai nel Calendar e imposta Start Year = 800** (mese 1, giorno 1). Poi ricontrolla che questo campo mostri `January 1, Year 800 CE`. Solo dopo le Era e i gate temporali funzionano.

---

**Mappatura dei campi rispetto a quello che ti ho dato**

Il form ha nomi diversi da quelli della guida:

| Nel mio file | Nel form reale |
|---|---|
| Description / Context Description | **Description** |
| Final Instructions | **Advanced Options → Location Writing Style & Tone** |
| Brief Context Description | **Key Activation → Brief Context Description** ✓ |

Quindi il blocco che chiamavo "Final Instructions" per Villa Douglas (controllo di Erik, griglia di Kaladin, affetto soffocante) va dentro **Location Writing Style & Tone**.

**Position:** il default è `After Character Definitions`, io avevo detto `In Chat`. Tieni il default — va bene e c'è un campo in meno da toccare.

**Character Limits:** default 0/5. Per Lunar Quad metti 2/6, per Villa Douglas 1/5, per Seven Hills 0/3.

**Simulation Overrides:** lascia tutto off. Marketplace, Purchasable Property e Jobs richiedono entry Lexicon che non esistono ancora — e comunque Villa Douglas non deve mai essere acquistabile: ci vivi perché sei una Douglas, non perché paghi.

**Recurring Activation:** `None` per tutte e tre. Serve per contenuti stagionali o notturni, che è roba da Calendario Sacro di Fenris, fase Lexicon.

**Timeline Start/End:** lasciali **off** anche su Lunar Quad finché non hai sistemato il calendario. Un gate con hour 0 sbagliato nasconderebbe la location senza dirti perché.

Prima un fatto che cambia il senso di questa route: ho controllato `Master_Design.md` e **Alyssa non vive a Villa Douglas** durante l'anno accademico. Vive in dormitorio al SUCC dal 28 agosto 2024 — Erik le ha approvato personalmente l'assegnazione, con *"a coincidental DCC security suite on the same floor"*.

Quindi questa non è la tratta casa-università quotidiana. È **il viaggio verso casa**: la distanza che separa la sua libertà dalla sorveglianza totale.

**Dati da inserire**

| Campo | Valore |
|---|---|
| **From** | `Villa Douglas` |
| **To** | `Lunar Quad` |
| **Travel Time (hours)** | `2` |
| **Distance (flavor)** | `Two hours of coast road` |
| **Hidden** | OFF |
| **Required Mediums** | `land` **+** `on foot` |
| **Route description** | vedi sotto |
| **Travel Requirements** | *(nessuno)* |

**Route description:**
```
La strada costiera tra Blackwood e Solarton. Due ore che separano il campus dalla villa: abbastanza perché Alyssa respiri, abbastanza vicino perché Malachia possa comparire senza preavviso.
```

**Perché 2 ore**

È una scelta di design, non un dato dai tuoi file (la distanza non è mai documentata). Il ragionamento: due ore sono lunghe abbastanza da rendere il viaggio un evento — non si torna a casa per caso — ma corte abbastanza da giustificare le *"casual terrifying drive-bys"* di Malachia citate nell'Arc 1. Se metti 30 minuti, Erik è sempre addosso e Solarton smette di funzionare come rifugio. Se metti 5 ore, la famiglia non può più irrompere e perdi il motore comico.

**Sul Required Medium: tieni anche "on foot"**

Realisticamente serve un'auto, quindi `land` è corretto. Ma se richiedi solo `land` e non hai ancora creato veicoli nel Lexicon, il giocatore potrebbe ritrovarsi **bloccato senza capire perché**. Per il primo test lascia entrambi attivi, poi togli `on foot` quando avrai i veicoli configurati — e a quel punto diventa una meccanica interessante: senza auto sei dipendente da chi te la offre, che nel tuo mondo significa dipendere da Logan o dalla DCC.

**Travel Requirements: lasciali vuoti**

Sono gate in stile Pokémon (badge, oggetti, allenatori sconfitti). Nel tuo mondo un domani potresti usarli — per esempio un requisito di Family Wanted Level per certe tratte — ma non ora.

**Una verifica importante**

Controlla che **Free Travel sia OFF** (l'interruttore in alto). Se è acceso, ogni location è raggiungibile istantaneamente da ovunque e la lista delle route viene ignorata completamente: la tua route esisterebbe senza avere alcun effetto.

summaries.summary: Riconsiderando il significato della distanza come libertà.
Rivalutò ubicazioni personaggi e stimò distanze tra città.

content.text:
Prima un fatto che cambia il senso di questa route: ho controllato `Master_Design.md` e **Alyssa non vive a Villa Douglas** durante l'anno accademico. Vive in dormitorio al SUCC dal 28 agosto 2024 — Erik le ha approvato personalmente l'assegnazione, con *"a coincidental DCC security suite on the same floor"*.

Quindi questa non è la tratta casa-università quotidiana. È **il viaggio verso casa**: la distanza che separa la sua libertà dalla sorveglianza totale.

**Dati da inserire**

| Campo | Valore |
|---|---|
| **From** | `Villa Douglas` |
| **To** | `Lunar Quad` |
| **Travel Time (hours)** | `2` |
| **Distance (flavor)** | `Two hours of coast road` |
| **Hidden** | OFF |
| **Required Mediums** | `land` **+** `on foot` |
| **Route description** | vedi sotto |
| **Travel Requirements** | *(nessuno)* |

**Route description:**
```
La strada costiera tra Blackwood e Solarton. Due ore che separano il campus dalla villa: abbastanza perché Alyssa respiri, abbastanza vicino perché Malachia possa comparire senza preavviso.
```

**Perché 2 ore**

È una scelta di design, non un dato dai tuoi file (la distanza non è mai documentata). Il ragionamento: due ore sono lunghe abbastanza da rendere il viaggio un evento — non si torna a casa per caso — ma corte abbastanza da giustificare le *"casual terrifying drive-bys"* di Malachia citate nell'Arc 1. Se metti 30 minuti, Erik è sempre addosso e Solarton smette di funzionare come rifugio. Se metti 5 ore, la famiglia non può più irrompere e perdi il motore comico.

**Sul Required Medium: tieni anche "on foot"**

Realisticamente serve un'auto, quindi `land` è corretto. Ma se richiedi solo `land` e non hai ancora creato veicoli nel Lexicon, il giocatore potrebbe ritrovarsi **bloccato senza capire perché**. Per il primo test lascia entrambi attivi, poi togli `on foot` quando avrai i veicoli configurati — e a quel punto diventa una meccanica interessante: senza auto sei dipendente da chi te la offre, che nel tuo mondo significa dipendere da Logan o dalla DCC.

**Travel Requirements: lasciali vuoti**

Sono gate in stile Pokémon (badge, oggetti, allenatori sconfitti). Nel tuo mondo un domani potresti usarli — per esempio un requisito di Family Wanted Level per certe tratte — ma non ora.

**Una verifica importante**

Controlla che **Free Travel sia OFF** (l'interruttore in alto). Se è acceso, ogni location è raggiungibile istantaneamente da ovunque e la lista delle route viene ignorata completamente: la tua route esisterebbe senza avere alcun effetto.

chat_messages.text:
La mappa risolve la questione, e cambia un po' i numeri.

**Cosa mostra la geografia**

Solarton è sulla costa, all'incirca dove starebbe Santa Barbara/Goleta, con SUCC appena a nord-est. Douglas Estate sta in alto, dentro il margine occidentale di Blackwood Forest, appena a ovest della Città di Blackwood. In mezzo c'è Hex Valley.

Il collegamento è una strada rossa che scende da Blackwood, costeggia il bordo orientale di Hex Valley e si innesta sulla 101 proprio all'altezza di SUCC. Non passa dalla costa.

Usando le città reali come scala (Santa Maria, Lompoc, Ventura, Oxnard sono tutte nelle posizioni corrette), la distanza è nell'ordine dei **130-145 km**. Ma è strada di montagna che aggira una valle, non autostrada.

**Valori aggiornati**

| Campo | Valore |
|---|---|
| Travel Time | `2` |
| Distance (flavor) | `90 miles of mountain road, then the 101` |

Le due ore reggono: su strada di crinale la media non supera i 65-70 km/h.

**La scoperta più interessante**

La mappa rivela che esistono **due percorsi possibili**, e il tuo lore li rende diversissimi:

1. **Interno** — Blackwood → bordo di Hex Valley → 101 a SUCC. Il più diretto.
2. **Costiero** — Blackwood → 101 verso Santa Maria → giù lungo la costa. Più lungo ma autostradale.

E qui torna una tua regola che avevi già scritto in `environments.md`: *"La Freeway 101 blocca fisicamente i lupi per via dell'inquinamento acustico e del traffico."*

Quindi la 101 non è solo una strada: è una **barriera per i lupi in forma non umana**. Un licantropo che vuole raggiungere Solarton correndo attraverso i boschi può farlo solo per la via interna, e comunque si ferma dove la 101 taglia il paesaggio.

Se vuoi sfruttarlo, la route su cui stai lavorando dovrebbe essere quella **interna**, e più avanti puoi aggiungerne una seconda dove il medium `on foot` è escluso proprio perché passa dalla freeway.

**Route description aggiornata:**
```
La strada interna che scende da Blackwood costeggiando Hex Valley e si innesta sulla 101 all'altezza del campus. Due ore di tornanti e bosco. È la sola via percorribile a quattro zampe: la 101 costiera è un muro di rumore e traffico che nessun lupo attraversa.
```

**Una nota sulla mappa**

Douglas Estate appare leggermente **fuori** dalla Città di Blackwood, nel bosco a ovest. È compatibile con Seven Hills come quartiere collinare sul lato foresta, ma tienilo presente quando scriverai le altre Location di Blackwood: la villa è al margine, non nel centro urbano.

chat_messages.text:
Questo cambia parecchio, ed è un dettaglio molto buono — perché una superstrada costruita dai Douglas non è infrastruttura, è **infrastruttura di controllo**.

Se l'hanno costruita loro, allora:

- È l'arteria che serve la DCC, non il campus. Il vero terminale è Los Angeles e la DCC Tower, non SUCC
- La sorveglianza ci vive sopra per default: telecamere, lettori di targhe, la griglia di Kaladin. Erik sa esattamente quando Alyssa la imbocca e in che direzione
- È veloce, perché una superstrada privata non ha tornanti da paese
- Ed è politicamente pesante: i Douglas hanno **asfaltato il territorio di Wulfnic** per fare business più in fretta. In un mondo dove i Firstborn considerano la modernità corporativa una degenerazione, questa strada è un'offesa fisica scritta nel paesaggio

**Valori aggiornati**

| Campo | Valore |
|---|---|
| Travel Time | `1` |
| Distance (flavor) | `90 miles on the Douglas Freeway` |

Un'ora, non due: è superstrada, non strada di montagna.

**Route description:**
```
La superstrada che i Douglas hanno fatto costruire per collegare Blackwood alla 101 e da lì a Los Angeles. Asfalto perfetto, quattro corsie che tagliano il bosco senza chiedere permesso a nessuno, e lettori di targhe della DCC a ogni svincolo. Un'ora di guida. Erik sa sempre chi la percorre e in che direzione.
```

**La conseguenza narrativa importante**

Un'ora sola significa che Erik può piombare al campus in tempi rapidissimi. Il che è ottimo per il tuo motore comico — l'estrazione tattica per un esame saltato diventa credibile — ma erode il cuscinetto di libertà di Alyssa.

Ecco perché ti conviene tenere **due route** verso Solarton:

1. **Douglas Freeway** — 1 ora, medium `land`, sorvegliata
2. **Vecchia strada interna / bosco** — 3 ore, medium `on foot` + `land`, nessuna copertura DCC

Così il giocatore ha una scelta reale: veloce e tracciato, oppure lento e invisibile. È esattamente il tipo di decisione che il tuo Family Wanted Level dovrebbe premiare o punire.

Se ti va, quando arriviamo alla seconda route te la preparo. Per ora inserisci la Freeway con questi valori.

Ma la domanda è buona, perché a regime questa route è **il** candidato naturale per un requisito.

**Cosa NON serve**

Un requisito "possiedi un'auto" via `Has Item` sarebbe ridondante: il **Required Medium `land`** fa già esattamente quello. Se il giocatore non ha un veicolo terrestre, la route è preclusa. Non duplicare la stessa regola in due posti.

**Cosa avrebbe senso più avanti**

Il Family Wanted Level. La logica narrativa è già scritta nei tuoi file: al livello 4 (Panic Grid) *"accounts are frozen"*, al livello 5 (Absolute Retrieval) Erik arriva di persona. Una superstrada privata con lettori di targhe DCC a ogni svincolo è esattamente il posto dove quel controllo si materializza.

Tradotto: sopra un certo FWL, la Douglas Freeway si chiude. Non perché ci sia un blocco fisico, ma perché imboccarla significa consegnarsi. E il giocatore è costretto sulla strada lenta nel bosco — che è precisamente la scelta interessante di cui parlavamo.

Non so se il campo `Custom` possa leggere i valori dell'InfoBoard. Il segnaposto mostra `_party.has_item.ID or quest.name.field`, quindi sono percorsi che leggono lo stato della party. **Route description:**
```
La vecchia strada da taglio che scende da Blackwood attraverso il margine di Hex Valley. Sterrato, tornanti, nessun lettore di targhe e nessun drone: la DCC non ha mai avuto motivo di sorvegliare una strada che non porta da nessuna parte.

Esisteva molto prima che i Douglas asfaltassero la superstrada. Molto prima che i Douglas esistessero. A quattro zampe la 101 resta un muro di rumore e traffico, tranne in un punto: il vecchio sottopasso all'altezza di Eorta, dove il bosco passa sotto l'asfalto e riemerge dall'altra parte, a pochi chilometri dal campus.

Tre ore. Nessuno sa che ci sei.
```

**Le tre scelte spiegate**

**Hidden ON** è la parte importante. La strada non compare nella lista delle destinazioni finché la narrazione non la rivela. È il tipo di cosa che Logan mostra ad Alyssa, o che Jasper scopre confrontando mappe DCC vecchie e nuove. Trasformi un'opzione di viaggio in un momento di trama.

**Il sottopasso di Eorta** risolve un problema di coerenza che sarebbe emerso comunque. La tua regola dice che *"La Freeway 101 blocca fisicamente i lupi"*, e SUCC è proprio sull'innesto della 101 — quindi un lupo che corre verso Solarton dovrebbe fermarsi al muro di rumore. Stabilendo **un solo punto di attraversamento**, la regola resta intatta e in più ottieni un luogo specifico e memorabile. Eorta compare sulla tua mappa in quella posizione.

**"Esisteva prima che i Douglas esistessero"** aggancia la route alla lore delle ere: Wulfnic tiene quel territorio dal ~1025, i Douglas arrivano nel 1666. La vecchia strada è di chi c'era prima.

**Il contrasto che hai creato**

| | Douglas Freeway | Old Logging Road |
|---|---|---|
| Tempo | 1 ora | 3 ore |
| Sorveglianza | totale | nessuna |
| Visibile | sempre | va scoperta |
| A quattro zampe | no | sì |

È una scelta reale, con un costo reale. Ed è il tipo di decisione che il Family Wanted Level dovrebbe registrare: prendere la freeway a FWL 4 significa consegnarsi.

**Una verifica**: controlla che il sistema accetti due route tra la stessa coppia di location. Se rifiuta il duplicato, la soluzione è creare un waypoint intermedio (es. una Location "Eorta Underpass") e spezzare la strada lenta in due tratte.

| **Required Mediums** | `on foot` **+** `land` |
| **Travel Requirements** | *(nessuno)* |

**Route description:**
```
La vecchia strada da taglio che scende da Blackwood attraverso il margine di Hex Valley. Sterrato, tornanti, nessun lettore di targhe e nessun drone: la DCC non ha mai avuto motivo di sorvegliare una strada che non porta da nessuna parte.

Esisteva molto prima che i Douglas asfaltassero la superstrada. Molto prima che i Douglas esistessero. A quattro zampe la 101 resta un muro di rumore e traffico, tranne in un punto: il vecchio sottopasso all'altezza di Eorta, dove il bosco passa sotto l'asfalto e riemerge dall'altra parte, a pochi chilometri dal campus.

Tre ore. Nessuno sa che ci sei.
```

**Le tre scelte spiegate**

**Hidden ON** è la parte importante. La strada non compare nella lista delle destinazioni finché la narrazione non la rivela. È il tipo di cosa che Logan mostra ad Alyssa, o che Jasper scopre confrontando mappe DCC vecchie e nuove. Trasformi un'opzione di viaggio in un momento di trama.

**Il sottopasso di Eorta** risolve un problema di coerenza che sarebbe emerso comunque. La tua regola dice che *"La Freeway 101 blocca fisicamente i lupi"*, e SUCC è proprio sull'innesto della 101 — quindi un lupo che corre verso Solarton dovrebbe fermarsi al muro di rumore. Stabilendo **un solo punto di attraversamento**, la regola resta intatta e in più ottieni un luogo specifico e memorabile. Eorta compare sulla tua mappa in quella posizione.

**"Esisteva prima che i Douglas esistessero"** aggancia la route alla lore delle ere: Wulfnic tiene quel territorio dal ~1025, i Douglas arrivano nel 1666. La vecchia strada è di chi c'era prima.

**Il contrasto che hai creato**

| | Douglas Freeway | Old Logging Road |
|---|---|---|
| Tempo | 1 ora | 3 ore |
| Sorveglianza | totale | nessuna |
| Visibile | sempre | va scoperta |
| A quattro zampe | no | sì |

È una scelta reale, con un costo reale. Ed è il tipo di decisione che il Family Wanted Level dovrebbe registrare: prendere la freeway a FWL 4 significa consegnarsi.

**Una verifica**: controlla che il sistema accetti due route tra la stessa coppia di location. Se rifiuta il duplicato, la soluzione è creare un waypoint intermedio (es. una Location "Eorta Underpass") e spezzare la strada lenta in due tratte.

input.file_text:
# World Introduction — Svartúlfr | Urban

Ingresso libero al mondo (senza scenario). Il giocatore crea la propria persona.

---

## Impostazioni base

| Campo | Valore |
|---|---|
| Custom world introduction | **ON** |
| **Default starting location** | **`Lunar Quad`** (non Villa Douglas) |
| Include Choose Your Character | **OFF** finché non esistono i personaggi |
| Include Build Your Stats | **ON** |
| Show "Begin here" to players | **ON** |

---

## World intro opening

```
Il quad è pieno. È sempre pieno.

Qualcuno ripassa ad alta voce sotto la Griffin Clocktower, qualcun altro dorme sullo zaino con la faccia al sole. Una ragazza con le corna discute di termodinamica. Un drago in maglietta scalda il caffè di qualcun altro soffiandoci sopra. Nessuno si volta. A Solarton non ci si volta.

Il sole californiano batte sull'asfalto e sull'erba calpestata, e sopra ogni cosa, troppo in alto perché un occhio umano lo noti, c'è il ronzio meccanico di qualcosa che gira in cerchio e non se ne va mai.

Benvenuto a SUCC. Il primo giorno del resto della tua vita, se sei il tipo che pensa in questi termini.

Io ti guardo da mille e duecento anni prima che questo prato esistesse. Vediamo cosa combini.
```

*(Voce di Wulfnic. Ultimo paragrafo = il narratore che si presenta senza nominarsi.)*

---

## Pages (in order)

### Pagina 1 — Info / Slide
**Titolo:** `Solarton e Blackwood`

```
La California ha due Città Libere, e sono legate come due mani intrecciate.

**Solarton** è la costa: sole, università, mare, trentacinquemila abitanti di ogni specie che convivono senza far domande. È il posto dove i soprannaturali possono fingere di essere normali.

**Blackwood** è l'entroterra: bosco antico, distretti governati dal Concilio, una città che si nasconde da quattrocento anni ed è brava a farlo. È il posto dove i soprannaturali smettono di fingere.

Tra le due corre una superstrada costruita dai Douglas, che i Douglas sorvegliano. E una vecchia strada nel bosco che i Douglas hanno dimenticato.
```

### Pagina 2 — Select (scenario field): Specie
**Titolo:** `Cosa sei`
**Field this page drives:** la domanda `species` (vedi Start questions)

### Pagina 3 — Select (scenario field): Legame
**Titolo:** `Perché sei qui`
**Field this page drives:** la domanda `tie`

### Pagina 4 — Build Stats
**Titolo:** `Cosa sai fare`

---

## Start questions

### Domanda 1 — `species`
| Campo | Valore |
|---|---|
| Tipo | Select |
| Label | `Cosa sei` |
| Subtitle | `Nessuno a Solarton te lo chiederà. Lo sentiranno.` |
| Required | ON |
| What this choice does | **Remember as variable** (`species`) + **Activate as lore** |

**Opzioni:**
```
Licantropo
Vampiro
Succube / Incubo
Umano (o quasi)
Altro
```

> Quando avrai il Lexicon, collega ogni opzione alla entry di specie corrispondente
> tramite "Activate as lore". Per ora basta Remember as variable.

### Domanda 2 — `tie`
| Campo | Valore |
|---|---|
| Tipo | Select |
| Label | `Perché sei a Solarton` |
| Required | ON |
| What this choice does | **Remember as variable** (`tie`) + **Set spawn location** |

**Opzioni e spawn:**
```
Matricola al SUCC        → Lunar Quad
Ci lavoro                → Lunar Quad
Vengo da Blackwood       → Seven Hills
Sono di passaggio        → Lunar Quad
```

> Aggiornerai gli spawn quando esisteranno più Location.

---

## Persona presets

### Preset 1
| Campo | Valore |
|---|---|
| Nome | `Matricola` |
| Suggested name | *(vuoto, lo sceglie il giocatore)* |
| Pronouns | *(qualsiasi)* |

```
Diciannove anni, primo semestre, valigia ancora mezza disfatta. Non conosci nessuno, non sai dove sia la Basilica Library, e hai già capito che il tuo compagno di stanza non dorme di notte. Va bene. Nessuno qui è quello che sembra, e questo ti include.
```

### Preset 2
| Campo | Valore |
|---|---|
| Nome | `Uno di Blackwood` |
| Pronouns | *(qualsiasi)* |

```
Sei cresciuto dalla parte sbagliata della superstrada, dove il Concilio conta più della legge e ogni famiglia ha un cognome che pesa. Solarton ti sembra finta: troppo sole, troppa gente che sorride. Sei qui per un motivo, e non è la laurea.
```

### Preset 3
| Campo | Valore |
|---|---|
| Nome | `Fuori posto` |
| Pronouns | *(qualsiasi)* |

```
Non appartieni a un branco, a una corte, a una famiglia. Sei arrivato da solo e resti da solo, e in un mondo costruito su gerarchie di sangue questo ti rende invisibile o interessante, a seconda di chi ti guarda.
```

---

## Stat templates

Base 1, max 10, budget 25. Ogni template distribuisce **31 punti totali**.

### Predatore
```
Descrizione: Forza, resistenza, un naso che non sbaglia. Risolvi le cose
             avvicinandoti.
```
| Might | Resilience | Agility | Wits | Presence | Scent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 6 | 5 | 3 | 4 | 6 |

### Notturno
```
Descrizione: Veloce, lucido, difficile da leggere. Vinci prima che il
             confronto cominci.
```
| Might | Resilience | Agility | Wits | Presence | Scent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 4 | 7 | 7 | 7 | 2 |

### Studioso
```
Descrizione: Fragile di corpo, temibile di testa. Sai cose che gli altri
             non sanno.
```
| Might | Resilience | Agility | Wits | Presence | Scent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 3 | 5 | 10 | 8 | 3 |

### Ammaliante
```
Descrizione: La presenza è la tua arma. Le stanze cambiano quando entri.
```
| Might | Resilience | Agility | Wits | Presence | Scent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 4 | 6 | 5 | 10 | 3 |

### Empatico
```
Descrizione: Senti tutto: paura, desiderio, menzogne. È un dono e una
             condanna.
```
| Might | Resilience | Agility | Wits | Presence | Scent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 |

---

## Da verificare

**Pages vs Start questions:** non è chiaro dalla documentazione se le pagine di tipo
"Select (scenario field)" consumino le Start questions o siano indipendenti. Testa con
una domanda sola prima di costruirne due.

**Macro nel World intro opening:** il campo supporta `{{memGet "<key>_name"}}`. Una
volta che `species` e `tie` sono salvate, puoi personalizzare l'apertura in base alle
scelte. Per ora l'ho lasciata generica perché l'apertura viene mostrata dopo le domande
e non sappiamo ancora se le variabili sono già disponibili a quel punto.

**Choose Your Character:** riaccendilo quando avrai creato Erik, Jasper, Noah ecc.

summary:
**Conversation Overview**

The user (screen name "Lys") is building a supernatural urban fantasy roleplay project called "Svartúlfr | Urban" set in Blackwood City, a werewolf-centric setting that is part of a larger cross-author collaborative universe combining three distinct settings: Underworld (Los Angeles), SUCC/Solarton (university setting), and Blackwood (the user's own Douglas family dynasty). The project uses Wyvern, a roleplay platform compatible with the chara_card_v2 JSON spec, and the user's goal throughout the conversation was to create polished character cards in JED+ format (a hybrid of bracketed attribute blocks and prose sections) for their main characters, plus supporting lorebook infrastructure.

Claude built or refined full character cards for Erik Douglas (Prime Alpha patriarch, billionaire CEO, grieving widower), Logan Douglas (Beta mechanic/club owner, his younger brother), and Malachia Douglas-Bloodmoon (eldest son, silent enforcer and underground fighter), plus standalone NPC reference materials for Magnus Douglas III and Elizabeth Duskwood-Douglas (Erik's parents) that were ultimately folded into lorebook entries rather than separate cards. Claude also converted two external lorebook files (Underworld.json and SUCC-U-VERSE.json) into the correct Wyvern chat-level lorebook schema, and built a mini test lorebook for a group chat test session. A canonical Wyvern schema template file was maintained and updated as new schema information was confirmed from real exports. Key lore decisions made during the conversation include: confirming Alyssa Douglas-Bloodmoon's "Species: Human" as a legacy error (she is a Founding Bloodline Dominant Omega and White Moon heir); establishing Kaladin Nargathon's full backstory as DCC Security Commander and Project BlackWolf veteran; confirming House Duskwood as a Pureblood werewolf house associated with grey wolves; establishing Erik's middle name as Cornelius (Magnus's choice); and confirming that in any lore conflict, official Underworld or SUCC material takes precedence over Blackwood/Douglas lore.

The user demonstrated several consistent working patterns: they prefer to review Claude's output critically before finalizing (flagging issues like Nixara's eye color, the hand wraps looping problem, and accessory over-fixation), they provide lore corrections and new canon in conversational chunks rather than structured documents, they want cards built from source files with discrepancies flagged and resolved with reasoning, and they prefer cards cleaned up and versioned iteratively rather than rebuilt from scratch. The user also confirmed a world calendar anchored at 1 January 800 AD 00:00 as world-age 0, and established that NPC dialogue in group chats must be prefixed with character name and colon for correct message splitting. For Wyvern's World interface fields, the user confirmed Level equals the character's canonical age, stat distribution uses a fixed 25-point budget regardless of level, HP maps to Resilience, and Mana maps to Presence.

content.text:
Keywords: You, your, yours, you're. Third-Person ("They"/"He"/"She"): The card describes the character objectively (e.g., "He is...", "Her history involves..."). Pros: Standard perspective for storytelling and literature, abundant in training data.

Creating effective Character Cards is not an exact science; the best approach can vary depending on the specific LLM (brand, size) and the desired outcome. However, several popular styles have emerged within the user community. Prose Style: One style involves writing the character description in natural prose, much like a narrative description in a book. This method requires careful writing to ensure clarity, avoid excessive keyword repetition, and maintain flow. It might be more challenging for beginners but potentially well-suited for users focused purely on narrative writing. List Formats: Another common approach uses list formats, where traits are categorized clearly. 

Variations exist, including: Simple Markdown lists (- item or * item). Wiki-style formatting (using templates or specific syntax like == Section ==). Community-created structured formats (like JED+ or W++).

However, based on my experience, highly structured but non-standard formats like W++ can sometimes lead to less consistent or coherent behavior (perhaps due to being less common in the LLM's training data). Similarly, directly pasting large amounts of raw text from a wiki ("wiki style") without curation can introduce irrelevant information ('bloat') and may not be optimally processed by the model. My current recommendation is something akin to JED+, which often involves a hybrid approach: using lists for concrete details like appearance and personality traits, and employing standard prose for background history or defining speech patterns. Regardless of style, it's essential to consider the writing perspective used within the card.

A character card is a file that defines who your AI character is. It contains the character’s name, personality description, dialogue style, first message, and any scenario or world lore you want to include.

Character cards follow the chara_card_v2 spec: a JSON object with a "spec" identifier and a "data" block containing name, description, personality, scenario, first_mes, and mes_example fields. PNG cards contain this same JSON embedded inside the image file. Newer versions of SillyTavern export chara_card_v3, which is backward compatible. ... Use PNG for sharing, since the character image and data travel together in one self-contained file, and every card site and frontend accepts it. JSON is useful when you want to edit the raw fields in a text editor or version control the card. SillyTavern imports both. How long does it take to make a SillyTavern character card? 

Writing the card definition takes 30-60 minutes for a quality card. The expressions step is where most people spend the most time - manually sourcing 28 consistent images can take hours.

content.title: Chat Mode | WyvernWiki
content.text:
The Main Chat Area is where the conversation happens. Everything you say and everything the character replies with will appear here, with your input box at the bottom. Each message appears in a bubble (or text box, or chat box, you get the idea), and each bubble has four buttons in the top right: ✏️ Edit – Change your message or the AI’s response. 🔃Rewind – Remove this message and everything after it. ⏩Continue – Ask the AI to add to the initial message, sending a longer response. 🔽 Collapse/Expand – Hide or reveal the full message (great for long responses). At the time of writing (August 5) the Branch button has been temporarily removed for bugfixing. It will return in the future. At the bottom of the screen is the text box where you type your message. You can press Enter to send it or click the Send button. 

Next to the input field is a three-dot icon (⋮) — click it to open extra options: 🤖 Impersonate Persona – Speak as your Persona rather than yourself ·

At first glance, the Chat Mode page might look a little overwhelming, especially with all the menus and buttons. But don’t worry, this guide will walk you through everything so you can chat like a pro. The Left Sidebar is your main navigation hub for picking who you want to chat with. From here, you can switch between characters, explore your sessions, and return to the main site. Each tab is marked with an icon. Here’s what they mean: 🕒 Rewinding Clock – Shows your most recent chats · 🔖 Bookmark – Displays characters you’ve bookmarked ... 👥 Group – Takes you to your group chat sessions, where you chat with multiple characters (and optionally, other users) Clicking on a character in any of these tabs will instantly load their chat in the main chat area. 

Tip: If you're on desktop, over over the icons if you forget what they mean.

1	# PART I — Species
     2	
     3	> This document describes the biology of the werewolf species: morphology, shift classes, blood classification, secondary sex physiology, life cycle, genetics, demographics, and reproduction. All content is strictly biological. Religious interpretations are flagged with "According to the Faith of Fenris..."
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## Morphology & Shift Classes
     8	
     9	Transformation is a biological characteristic of the species, independent of rank, religion, or culture. Every werewolf possesses three distinct morphological states.
    10	
    11	### Partial Shift
    12	
    13	The daily form. A voluntary or emotionally triggered manifestation of lupine traits over the baseline humanoid body.
    14	
    15	- Visible features: ears, tail, eyes, teeth, claws.
    16	- Activation: voluntary or emotional (stress, arousal, aggression).
    17	- Primary use: communication, intimidation, body language, social signaling.
    18	- Cognitive capacity: fully human.
    19	- This is the form most werewolves present in everyday life within their own communities.
    20	
    21	---
    22	
    23	### Hybrid Shift — Species True Form
    24	
    25	The true biological form of the werewolf. The "human" appearance is a mimetic adaptation; the Hybrid is what the species actually is.
    26	
    27	- Bipedal digitigrade stance.
    28	- Full fur coverage matching hair color.
    29	- Maximum physical strength and sensory acuity.
    30	- Full cognitive capacity retained.
    31	- Speech and language fully maintained.
    32	- This form is used for combat, serious pack business, formal ceremonies, and situations requiring full biological capability.
    33	
    34	> **LSE Design Note:** The Hybrid Shift is the _Species True Form_. The humanoid appearance is a survival adaptation for coexistence with humans, not the "default" state.
    35	
    36	---
    37	
    38	### Full Shift
    39	
    40	The quadrupedal wolf form. A complete transformation into a large wolf.
    41	
    42	- Specialized for: hunting, pursuit, long-distance travel, pack combat formations.
    43	- Cognitive capacity: retained but communication shifts to non-verbal (body language, scent, vocalizations).
    44	- Physical profile: larger than a natural wolf, size varies by individual and blood classification.
    45	
    46	> **LSE Design Note:** Full Shift is **not** inherently "more powerful" than Hybrid Shift. It is _specialized_. A Hybrid fighter in close quarters may outperform a Full Shift wolf, while a Full Shift wolf excels in open terrain pursuit. This avoids the "Full Wolf = Super Saiyan" trope.
    47	
    48	---
    49	
    50	## Blood Classification
    51	
    52	Blood Classification is a genetic taxonomy describing an individual's lineage relative to the species' origin. It is immutable and determined by birth.
    53	
    54	| Classification | Definition | Characteristics |
    55	|---|---|---|
    56	| **Divine Blood** | The Nine Firstborn. According to the Faith of Fenris, created directly by the First Wolf. Recorded History confirms their existence but not the mechanism of their origin. | Biological immortality, extreme regeneration, perfect transformation stability, supreme pheromonal aura, absolute Command. |
    57	| **Founding Bloodlines** | Direct children and grandchildren of the Firstborn. Founders of the Great Houses. | Exceptionally long lifespan, high genetic stability, strong Command affinity, enhanced regeneration. |
    58	| **Pureblood Houses** | Multi-generational descendants of Founding Bloodlines. The aristocracy. | Long lifespan, stable genetics, reliable secondary sex expression, strong pack bonds. |
    59	| **Common Bloodlines** | The majority of the werewolf population. | Standard werewolf biology. Lifespan, strength, and abilities within normal species range. |
    60	| **Modified Lineages** | Individuals whose genetics have been artificially altered through experimentation, forced transformation, or technological intervention. | Unpredictable traits. May include enhanced abilities, instability, feral tendencies, or shortened lifespan. (e.g., Gamma-7 program subjects.) |
    61	
    62	> **Cross-reference:** The historical context of who belongs to each classification — particularly the Nine Firstborn — is documented in [LSE_06_History.md](LSE_06_History.md) and [LSE_07_Foundational_Figures.md](LSE_07_Foundational_Figures.md).
    63	
    64	---
    65	
    66	## Secondary Sex Physiology
    67	
    68	Secondary sex is determined biologically at Presentation (typically around age 13). It is immutable. There are five secondary sexes (Alpha, Delta, Beta, Omega, Enigma), with the Enigma being so extraordinarily rare (~1 per generation, may skip) that it is excluded from general population statistics and often described as a "sacred caste." All individuals are in the Gamma state prior to Presentation.
    69	
    70	### Age of Maturation
    71	
    72	Most individuals present their secondary sex at approximately 13 years of age, entering a maturation period that can last into the late teens or early twenties. After maturation concludes, they are considered full adults.
    73	
    74	---
    75	
    76	### γ Gamma — Pre-Presentation State
    77	
    78	**Description:** Gamma is not a secondary sex. It is the **neutral developmental state** of all werewolves prior to Presentation. Every werewolf is biologically Gamma from birth until their secondary sex emerges (typically around age 13). Pre-presentation, the child's future secondary sex is unknown; most are referred to with neutral pronouns such as Ze, Zer, and Zim until Presentation.
    79	
    80	**Biology:** A Gamma child possesses both sets of genitalia — a vaginal opening with a penile structure in place of the clitoris — and a uterus. At Presentation, this anatomy resolves: if the individual presents as Omega (male), the uterus develops fully; if they present as Alpha (female), the uterus remains mostly vestigial/non-functional. The external genitalia differentiate accordingly.
    81	
    82	**Statistics:** 100% of werewolves are Gamma pre-Presentation. Post-Presentation, 0% remain Gamma — it is a transient state, not a permanent classification.
    83	
    84	---
    85	
    86	### ∑ Enigma — The Sacred Caste
    87	
    88	**Description:** The Enigma is a legitimate secondary sex — simply so extraordinarily rare (~1 per generation, may skip) that it is excluded from general population statistics. Enigmas are the apex of the species' biological potential.
    89	
    90	There are two recognized types:
    91	
    92	- **Primordial Enigma:** The Nine Firstborn. Unique beings whose origin, according to the Faith of Fenris, was divine. They cannot be replicated or reproduced. Their biology transcends the normal species parameters.
    93	- **Ascended Enigma:** Exceptionally rare individuals (~10 in recorded history across two millennia) who present with Enigma-level biological traits despite having no Divine Blood lineage. Their emergence is unpredictable and not fully understood. **Important demographic note:** Due to the extreme hormonal dominance of the Enigma pheromonal signature, if an Enigma is present and active on a given continent, no other individual will typically present as Enigma — the Enigma's presence suppresses Enigma-expression in others until their passing or departure.
    94	
    95	**Characteristics:** Mirror Alpha behavior but with superior intensity. Cannot be submitted by any other secondary sex. Can dominate all genders, including Alphas. Possess Command that cannot be resisted by any standard secondary sex. Superior strength, intelligence, and pheromonal presence.
    96	
    97	**Biology:** Identical to Alpha biology in structure, but their scent cannot be overridden even by an Omega in heat. They can resist the call of an Omega in heat. An Enigma can impregnate every gender with a reproductive system. The Command of an Enigma cannot be resisted by standard secondary sexes; only a Dominant Omega may resist, depending on willpower.
    98	
    99	**Statistics:** An Enigma is born approximately once per generation. Sometimes it skips a generation entirely.
   100	
   101	---
   102	
   103	### α Alpha — The Protector
   104	
   105	**Description:** In the pack, an Alpha is biologically predisposed to be territorial, protective, and competitive, with highly developed pheromonal presence. However, **Alpha ≠ Leader**. Being an Alpha does not mean they automatically lead the pack; it simply means they have the biological instincts of a guardian and enforcer. Not all leaders are Alphas, and not all Alphas become leaders.
   106	
   107	**Characteristics:** Usually taller, broader, and physically stronger. Aggressive by nature when threatened. Highly territorial. Strong orientation toward leadership or frontline defense. While they can use the _Command_ to influence others, their role in the pack depends entirely on their designated social rank. They can be excellent warriors or protectors while answering to a Beta or Delta Pack Leader.
   108

# PART I — Species

> This document describes the biology of the werewolf species: morphology, shift classes, blood classification, secondary sex physiology, life cycle, genetics, demographics, and reproduction. All content is strictly biological. Religious interpretations are flagged with "According to the Faith of Fenris..."

---

## Morphology & Shift Classes

Transformation is a biological characteristic of the species, independent of rank, religion, or culture. Every werewolf possesses three distinct morphological states.

### Partial Shift

The daily form. A voluntary or emotionally triggered manifestation of lupine traits over the baseline humanoid body.

- Visible features: ears, tail, eyes, teeth, claws.
- Activation: voluntary or emotional (stress, arousal, aggression).
- Primary use: communication, intimidation, body language, social signaling.
- Cognitive capacity: fully human.
- This is the form most werewolves present in everyday life within their own communities.

---

### Hybrid Shift — Species True Form

The true biological form of the werewolf. The "human" appearance is a mimetic adaptation; the Hybrid is what the species actually is.

- Bipedal digitigrade stance.
- Full fur coverage matching hair color.
- Maximum physical strength and sensory acuity.
- Full cognitive capacity retained.
- Speech and language fully maintained.
- This form is used for combat, serious pack business, formal ceremonies, and situations requiring full biological capability.

> **LSE Design Note:** The Hybrid Shift is the _Species True Form_. The humanoid appearance is a survival adaptation for coexistence with humans, not the "default" state.

---

### Full Shift

The quadrupedal wolf form. A complete transformation into a large wolf.

- Specialized for: hunting, pursuit, long-distance travel, pack combat formations.
- Cognitive capacity: retained but communication shifts to non-verbal (body language, scent, vocalizations).
- Physical profile: larger than a natural wolf, size varies by individual and blood classification.

> **LSE Design Note:** Full Shift is **not** inherently "more powerful" than Hybrid Shift. It is _specialized_. A Hybrid fighter in close quarters may outperform a Full Shift wolf, while a Full Shift wolf excels in open terrain pursuit. This avoids the "Full Wolf = Super Saiyan" trope.

---

## Blood Classification

Blood Classification is a genetic taxonomy describing an individual's lineage relative to the species' origin. It is immutable and determined by birth.

| Classification | Definition | Characteristics |
|---|---|---|
| **Divine Blood** | The Nine Firstborn. According to the Faith of Fenris, created directly by the First Wolf. Recorded History confirms their existence but not the mechanism of their origin. | Biological immortality, extreme regeneration, perfect transformation stability, supreme pheromonal aura, absolute Command. |
| **Founding Bloodlines** | Direct children and grandchildren of the Firstborn. Founders of the Great Houses. | Exceptionally long lifespan, high genetic stability, strong Command affinity, enhanced regeneration. |
| **Pureblood Houses** | Multi-generational descendants of Founding Bloodlines. The aristocracy. | Long lifespan, stable genetics, reliable secondary sex expression, strong pack bonds. |
| **Common Bloodlines** | The majority of the werewolf population. | Standard werewolf biology. Lifespan, strength, and abilities within normal species range. |
| **Modified Lineages** | Individuals whose genetics have been artificially altered through experimentation, forced transformation, or technological intervention. | Unpredictable traits. May include enhanced abilities, instability, feral tendencies, or shortened lifespan. (e.g., Gamma-7 program subjects.) |

> **Cross-reference:** The historical context of who belongs to each classification — particularly the Nine Firstborn — is documented in [LSE_06_History.md](LSE_06_History.md) and [LSE_07_Foundational_Figures.md](LSE_07_Foundational_Figures.md).

---

## Secondary Sex Physiology

Secondary sex is determined biologically at Presentation (typically around age 13). It is immutable. There are five secondary sexes (Alpha, Delta, Beta, Omega, Enigma), with the Enigma being so extraordinarily rare (~1 per generation, may skip) that it is excluded from general population statistics and often described as a "sacred caste." All individuals are in the Gamma state prior to Presentation.

### Age of Maturation

Most individuals present their secondary sex at approximately 13 years of age, entering a maturation period that can last into the late teens or early twenties. After maturation concludes, they are considered full adults.

---

### γ Gamma — Pre-Presentation State

**Description:** Gamma is not a secondary sex. It is the **neutral developmental state** of all werewolves prior to Presentation. Every werewolf is biologically Gamma from birth until their secondary sex emerges (typically around age 13). Pre-presentation, the child's future secondary sex is unknown; most are referred to with neutral pronouns such as Ze, Zer, and Zim until Presentation.

**Biology:** A Gamma child possesses both sets of genitalia — a vaginal opening with a penile structure in place of the clitoris — and a uterus. At Presentation, this anatomy resolves: if the individual presents as Omega (male), the uterus develops fully; if they present as Alpha (female), the uterus remains mostly vestigial/non-functional. The external genitalia differentiate accordingly.

**Statistics:** 100% of werewolves are Gamma pre-Presentation. Post-Presentation, 0% remain Gamma — it is a transient state, not a permanent classification.

---

### ∑ Enigma — The Sacred Caste

**Description:** The Enigma is a legitimate secondary sex — simply so extraordinarily rare (~1 per generation, may skip) that it is excluded from general population statistics. Enigmas are the apex of the species' biological potential.

There are two recognized types:

- **Primordial Enigma:** The Nine Firstborn. Unique beings whose origin, according to the Faith of Fenris, was divine. They cannot be replicated or reproduced. Their biology transcends the normal species parameters.
- **Ascended Enigma:** Exceptionally rare individuals (~10 in recorded history across two millennia) who present with Enigma-level biological traits despite having no Divine Blood lineage. Their emergence is unpredictable and not fully understood. **Important demographic note:** Due to the extreme hormonal dominance of the Enigma pheromonal signature, if an Enigma is present and active on a given continent, no other individual will typically present as Enigma — the Enigma's presence suppresses Enigma-expression in others until their passing or departure.

**Characteristics:** Mirror Alpha behavior but with superior intensity. Cannot be submitted by any other secondary sex. Can dominate all genders, including Alphas. Possess Command that cannot be resisted by any standard secondary sex. Superior strength, intelligence, and pheromonal presence.

**Biology:** Identical to Alpha biology in structure, but their scent cannot be overridden even by an Omega in heat. They can resist the call of an Omega in heat. An Enigma can impregnate every gender with a reproductive system. The Command of an Enigma cannot be resisted by standard secondary sexes; only a Dominant Omega may resist, depending on willpower.

**Statistics:** An Enigma is born approximately once per generation. Sometimes it skips a generation entirely.

---

### α Alpha — The Protector

**Description:** In the pack, an Alpha is biologically predisposed to be territorial, protective, and competitive, with highly developed pheromonal presence. However, **Alpha ≠ Leader**. Being an Alpha does not mean they automatically lead the pack; it simply means they have the biological instincts of a guardian and enforcer. Not all leaders are Alphas, and not all Alphas become leaders.

**Characteristics:** Usually taller, broader, and physically stronger. Aggressive by nature when threatened. Highly territorial. Strong orientation toward leadership or frontline defense. While they can use the _Command_ to influence others, their role in the pack depends entirely on their designated social rank. They can be excellent warriors or protectors while answering to a Beta or Delta Pack Leader.

**Biology:** Alpha scent glands produce aggressive, oppressive pheromones that can control a room of Betas, Deltas, and Omegas. Through scent, they communicate intent and mood. A true Command (combining pheromones, will, and spoken word) forces compliance from Betas and Omegas; Deltas may or may not resist depending on will. Most Alphas are immune to another Alpha's Command.

An Alpha's penis features the bulbous glandis (knot) at its base, which inflates during intercourse to lock with a partner and maximize conception chances. Additionally, male Alphas of Pureblood, Founding, or Divine bloodlines possess a baculum (os penis), a trait absent in Common and Modified bloodlines.

Alphas enter rut approximately monthly, lasting 3–10 days. During rut, pheromones intensify and behavior becomes more aggressive, but unlike most Omegas, Alphas can generally control their rut without disrupting society.

< truncated lines 115-277 >

### Stress Cycles

Extreme upheaval or stress can trigger an unexpected heat or rut. This is theorized to be a biological mechanism to rally pack support and comfort.

### Feral State

Triggered by life-threatening stress or extreme overwhelm. Instinct takes complete control. Can usually be calmed by a packmate. Packless individuals require specialized care.

---

## Bonding

Bonds are links connecting one individual to another, often involving a physical claim on a scent gland that creates a mental/emotional link where both parties can feel each other's emotions. Bonds can be shielded (temporarily blocking emotional transmission).

### Bond Types

| Type | Location | Duration | Breaking |

| **Parental** | Back of pup's neck | Permanent unless extreme abuse/neglect | Dangerous. Very difficult. |
| **Romantic** | Neck / upper collarbone | Fades after ~3 years without reinforcement | Extremely dangerous. Can cause illness or death. |
| **Platonic** | Wrists | Fades as relationship weakens | Relatively safe. Minor sickness possible. |
| **Sexual** | Inner thighs | 3 days to 1 week | Easy. Natural. |
| **Pack** | No physical claim required | Permanent unless extreme abuse/neglect | Very dangerous. Triggers dangerous mating cycle. |

---

## Scent Glands

Scent glands are skin areas that hold and release pheromone-carrying secretions. Their location, sensitivity, and function vary by secondary sex and age.

### By Secondary Sex

**Enigmas & Alphas:** Most extensive coverage. Strongest glands on neck, shoulders, and inner thighs. Also present on fingers and torso (risking accidental scenting). Greatest conscious control over scent output.

**Omegas:** Most sensitive and reactive glands. Billions of nerve connections for instant pheromonal response. Inner thigh and neck glands as sensitive as lips or genitals (depending on cycle stage). Breast and stomach glands develop during pregnancy.

**Deltas & Betas:** Weakest scent glands but hold scents longer. Strongest on neck, inner thighs, and behind ears.

**Pups:** Base-level scent glands that develop at presentation. Strongest gland on crown of head. Cannot hold scent long — requires constant parental scenting.

### Specific Gland Locations

| Location | Social Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Inner Thighs** | Mates/partners only. Without consent = assault. On pups = criminal. | Can trigger heat/rut if aggressively scented. |
| **Crown of Head** | "Pup's Crown." Most sensitive in childhood, fades with age. | |
| **Wrists** | Most respectful scenting location. Friends, first dates. | Rubbing wrist glands = anxiety sign. Pack bites placed here. |
| **Cheeks** | Similar respect level to wrists. Common among pup friends. | Minor scent production. |
| **Neck** | Most sensitive for all dynamics. Mating bite location. | Holds scent longest. Parental bonds on nape. |

---

**Statistics:** 1 in 10 individuals.

---

### δ Delta — The Engine

**Description:** Deltas are the true "engine" of the pack. They patrol, coordinate, assist with pups, teach, mediate, and lead hunts. They are naturally suited for roles such as vice-leader, scout, tactician, field commander, or instructor. They are not simply "weaker Alphas" — they are the highly coordinated, active core of pack operations.

**Characteristics:** Physically comparable to Alphas. Highly cooperative and strategic. Excel in dynamic environments, bridging the gap between the protective instincts of Alphas and the administrative focus of Betas. Thrive in active duty — border patrols, coordinated hunts, field operations.

**Biology:** Nearly identical to Alpha biology, including the presence of a baculum (os penis) strictly in Founding or Divine bloodlines. The key difference: Deltas are unable to form true Commands.

**Statistics:** 1 in 15 individuals.

---

### β Beta — The Social Glue

**Description:** Betas are the social glue of the pack. They maintain territory, construct, administer, manage resources, cook, raise young, act as artisans, and trade. They are the fundamental workers who allow the pack to function day-to-day.

**Characteristics:** Peaceful, cooperative, highly skilled in specialized areas. Strong communal mentality. Share knowledge and resources to ensure pack stability. An older Beta may serve as Pack Leader due to organizational skills.

Betas are a balance of typical Omega and Alpha instincts (nurture and protection), though their instincts are weaker than either. This balance makes them powerful social adapters — they can appeal to all secondary sexes because they understand the instincts of both Omegas and Alphas without being dominated by them.

**Biology:** Scent glands at the base of neck and wrists. Beta scent is much more subdued than Alpha, Delta, or Omega. For Betas, primary gender plays a larger biological role than for Alphas or Omegas. Female Betas experience monthly bleeding lasting 3 days to a week. Male Betas of Founding or Divine bloodlines possess a baculum (os penis), a trait absent in Common, Modified, and Pureblood lines.

Betas cannot have naturally occurring heats or ruts but can have medically induced minor cycles (M.I.H./M.I.R.) — most often used to assist mates during mating cycles.

**Statistics:** 1 in 1,500 individuals.

> **Note:** Betas have their own personal spaces (office, entertainment corner, hammock) rather than dens or nests. They hum softly and sigh deeply when content.

---

### Ω Omega — The Emotional Regulator

**Description:** Omegas are the crucial emotional regulators of the pack. They possess extremely high empathy, calming pheromones, and a strong instinct to care for others. They create social cohesion and are vital during crises. They are **not** sexually submissive by definition.

**Characteristics:** Physically more agile and softer in appearance. During pack stress or crisis, the Omega reduces tensions, protects pups, and keeps the pack united. Their pheromones soothe aggressive Alphas and Deltas. They serve as the emotional anchor of the family. An elder Omega often acts as primary advisor to the Pack Leader.

**Biology:** Scent glands at the base of neck and wrists. Omega scent is floral, sweet, and highly appealing. Can overpower Beta scents but never Alpha scents unless in heat.

Omegas are very fertile (99% during heat). Before heat, they experience pre-heat (up to a week), during which their scent gradually intensifies and they prepare their nest. Heat lasts 3–10 days. During heat, most Omegas are incoherent and driven by breeding instinct — decisions made during heat are considered non-consensual.

Post-heat, the Omega is tired and sluggish, consuming large meals to rebalance energy.

**Statistics:** 1 in 30 individuals.

---

### Subgenders

Both Alpha and Omega have subgender variants that emerge during maturation:

**Alpha Subgenders:**
- **Dominant Alpha:** A mix of Enigma and standard Alpha traits. More powerful but less likely to find a mate. Overprotective of partners.
- **Submissive Alpha:** Raised in warm, nurturing environments. Devoted caregivers. Unlikely to be unfaithful. Fiercely protective of children regardless of biological parentage.

**Omega Subgenders:**
- **Dominant Omega:** The second-rarest rank. Known as "Legend of The Unsubmitted" -- can resist Alpha and Enigma Commands. Only fully submits to their mate (Dominant Alpha or Enigma). Compliance may depend on mood.

  The rarest expression of the Dominant Omega is known as **the White Moon**: a Dominant Omega of Founding Bloodline or higher whose pacification gift reaches continental-bloodline intensity -- capable of instinctively stilling the aggression of Alphas and Enigmas within proximity without a spoken word. The White Moon title is not a political rank but a religious and biological designation recognized by Moon Speakers. According to the Faith of Fenris, a White Moon Dominant Omega is the species' emotional sovereign: the Unsubmitted One who holds the pack together when it fractures. The title is conferred by the Living Sagas (or, in their absence, by unanimous Moon Speaker recognition) and is never self-declared.

  **White Moon biology:** The White Moon's pacification response is involuntary and ambient -- a passive pheromonal field that reads dominant threat-states and responds with Omega-class calming chemistry at anomalous intensity. They are immune to Alpha Command and Enigma Command alike. Their heat cycle is unaffected by this ability. They cannot be compelled, but they can be overwhelmed by sensory phobia (loud noise, aggressive physical contact) -- the ability does not confer combat capability.

  **White Moon pack role:** In pack theory (LSE_03_Civilization), the White Moon occupies the functional apex of the Omega caste not through authority but through necessity: where an ordinary Dominant Omega soothes the immediate pack, a White Moon stabilizes multi-pack or politically fractured situations. Historically, every documented White Moon has been the mate or recognized spiritual partner of the ruling Enigma -- not by law, but by biological complementarity. The Faith of Fenris calls this pairing "the King and the Moon."

  **Rarity:** One White Moon per bloodline generation at most. Many generations produce none. The title has never been documented in a Common Bloodline individual.

- **Submissive Omega:** Extended heats, more attractive to Alphas, more susceptible to assault. More nurturing and sensitive than standard Omegas. Typically prefers a Dominant Alpha as a consensual partner.

---

## Procreation Capability

| Category | Can Impregnate | Can Be Impregnated |
|---|---|---|
| Enigmas | ✓ All genders with reproductive system | ✗ |
| Male Alphas | ✓ | ✗ |
| Male Betas / Male Deltas | ✓ | Only by Enigma |
| Female Alphas / Male Omegas (Dom/Normal) / Female Deltas | ✓ | ✓ |
| Female Betas / Female Omegas / Submissive Omegas | ✗ | ✓ |

---

## Life Cycle

Every werewolf passes through the following developmental stages. Each stage affects hormones, social role, fertility, behavior, and physical capability.

| Stage | Approximate Age | Key Characteristics |
|---|---|---|
| **Infant** | 0–2 | Helpless. Entirely dependent on parents and pack. Strongest scent gland on crown of head. |
| **Pup** | 2–12 | Learning social bonds, language, and basic pack skills. High emotional intelligence. Forms school packs. Constant scenting by parents required. |
| **Juvenile** | 12–14 | Presentation occurs (~13). Secondary sex emerges. Maturation begins. First heat/rut (cannot be suppressed). |
| **Adolescent** | 14–17 | Maturation continues. Subgender expression stabilizes. Training in pack roles begins. |
| **Young Adult** | 17–22 | The Call of the Pack: choose to stay or disperse. First independent pack roles assigned. Courtship begins. |
| **Adult** | 22–40 | Full maturity. Peak fertility. Active profession and pack role. |
| **Prime** | 40–60 | Peak authority and experience. Often in leadership positions. |
| **Elder** | 60–100+ | Advisor and wisdom-keeper. Reduced fertility. High social respect. |
| **Ancestor** | 100+ (rare) | Living repositories of history and culture. Venerated by the pack. Extremely rare outside Pureblood and Founding Bloodlines. |

> **Note:** Lifespan varies dramatically by Blood Classification. Common Bloodlines may live 80–150 years. Pureblood Houses can reach 200–400 years. Founding Bloodlines may exceed 500 years. Divine Blood individuals have achieved biological immortality (1,000+ years confirmed).

---

## Genetics

The werewolf genome is organized in layers of increasing specificity:

```
Werewolf Genome
├── Species Genes        — Defines the species (shift capability, regeneration, scent glands, pheromone production)
├── Pack Genes           — Regional/bloodline adaptations (fur color, scent profile, environmental tolerance)
├── Secondary Sex Genes  — Determines Alpha/Delta/Beta/Omega expression at presentation
└── Individual Traits    — Unique characteristics (eye color, height, specific talents, personality predispositions)
```

This genetic architecture opens the door to:
- **Mutations:** Rare genetic variations producing unexpected traits.
- **Bloodline Traits:** Specific abilities or physical characteristics associated with particular Houses.
- **Genetic Diseases:** Conditions specific to the species.
- **Hybrids:** Offspring of werewolves with other supernatural species (extremely rare and controversial).

---

## Reproduction

### Heat Cycle (Omega)

- **Frequency:** Every 3 months.
- **Duration:** 3–10 days.
- **Pre-heat:** Up to 1 week. Scent intensifies. Nest preparation. Coherent decision-making.
- **Active Heat:** Incoherent. Driven by breeding instinct. Decisions made during heat are non-consensual.
- **Post-heat:** Fatigue, increased appetite, energy rebalancing.
- **Asexual Heats:** Can be satisfied through cuddling, scent proximity, and emotional intimacy without sexual intercourse. Asexuals often lack slick production.

### Rut Cycle (Alpha)

- **Frequency:** Monthly, or triggered by Omega heat pheromones.
- **Duration:** 3–10 days.
- **Effects:** Intensified pheromones, increased aggression. Generally controllable without societal disruption.
- **Detection:** An Alpha in rut can potentially detect an Omega's pregnancy by scenting the neck.

### Sympathy Cycles

When a packmate enters heat or rut, same-dynamic packmates may experience sympathy cycles. Common around newly-presenting pups or during stress cycles.

I'm noticing a real inconsistency here: Erik's card implies {{user}} is Jasper's twin, but Nixara's card explicitly names Alyssa as the twin born with Jasper and lists her four children without including {{user}} at all. This suggests {{user}} is likely meant as a separate character distinct from Nixara's canonical family, not literally her twin child.

I want to check Alyssa's own card to see whether she's meant as a separate developed sister or whether {{user}} is designed to occupy her narrative role — this feels like a genuine continuity conflict worth flagging, since both can't simultaneously be "the twin born with Jasper."

I'm also noting several missing lore threads: Nixara's rare White Moon Dominant Omega status and Erik surviving a Caccia-confirmed Mate Bond break, which per canon is nearly fatal and would explain the depth of Erik's trauma; Wulfnic's historic Anointing of Nixara as the first in centuries; and the missing marriage date. I should also revisit how the card handles Alpha Command compared to the more nuanced canon description of forced compliance across designations.

The card doesn't currently mention Erik's rut cycle details from canon (monthly, 3-10 days, scent-based pregnancy detection), which matters for consistency in intimate scenes. I'm also noticing Villa Douglas is underdeveloped compared to Nixara's richer file, which has the exact address, Clan Seal, and architectural details worth incorporating.

Beyond that, I want to verify the security grid names, PMC commanders, and Erik's den name against the source lore, plus cross-check the Douglas family tree in the Dinastie file for correct birth order and Alyssa's placement before moving to the World_Seed and Guide_World documents.…

content.thinking:
This is a huge find — the master genealogy identifies Alyssa as "Founding Bloodline, Dominant Omega (White Moon)," a werewolf and confirmed heir to the White Moon title after Nixara, which directly contradicts Alyssa.md's claim that she's human. That's a genuine continuity conflict between the two files.

Actually this reads as an intentional narrative twist: Alyssa believes herself fully human (per her persona card), unaware her family is concealing her true nature as heir to the White Moon lineage. This gives Erik's overprotection a much deeper grounding — he's not just paranoid, he likely knows or suspects his daughter carries this destiny and is desperately hiding/shielding her from it.

I notice this thread is entirely absent from Erik's card, which makes it a critical gap worth flagging. It also raises a genealogy contradiction: the master table lists her as "Dominant Omega (White Moon)" while Alyssa's own card lists her Species as Human — possibly because she hasn't presented yet, or because her family conceals her lupine nature to protect her from the danger tied to that title.

Beyond that, there's a naming inconsistency around "Kaladin" — Erik and Alyssa's cards call him "Kaladin Nargathon," Nixara's card gives no surname for him, and the Dinastie key lists "Kaladin Ashwood," so three different identities are floating around for what should be one character.

Marcus Thornfield's role holds up consistently across Alyssa's card and Nixara's mentions as PMC lead / Head of Executive Protection ("Iron"). Villa Douglas has richer details worth folding into Erik's card — the exact address, Clan Seal, biological architecture, and its designation as Erik's Sanctuary. And I'm noticing a potential conflict in Blackwood City's founding lore: the 1666 treaty between the Douglas clan and Wulfnic Bloodmoon versus the Dinastie file's separate account of the Järn-Gildi Norse clan's origins.

This looks like a broader pattern too — Wulfnic "Ulfr," Logi "Logan," Magnus "Malachia," Njal "Noah" all seem to be Norse-era ancestral analogues to the modern family, suggesting a dual-timeline reincarnation or parallel-universe lore layer running across the setting's variant worlds.…

content.text:
Ho riletto la lore completa (Card_Erik, Tier2 entries, LSE, Nixara, Alyssa, Dinastia Bloodmoon-Douglas) e ci sono cose interessanti — sia problemi da sistemare che materiale forte da aggiungere.

**Elemento critico #1 — contraddizione su {{user}}/Alyssa**
Il file `Alyssa.md` (persona di {{user}}) dice `Species(Human)`. Ma la genealogia master (`Dinastie_Bloodmoon_Douglas.json`) e il lorebook di Nixara dicono che {{user}}/Alyssa è **Founding Bloodline, Dominant Omega — ed erede del titolo di White Moon** dopo Nixara, con "immunità assoluta all'Alpha Command" e "una destinazione terrificante che vuole disperatamente evitare." Sono due verità incompatibili sulla stessa entità, a meno che non sia intenzionale (Alyssa cresciuta credendosi umana, verità nascosta anche a lei). Se è voluto, è oro narrativo per Erik — vuol dire che lui potrebbe sapere/sospettare la vera natura della figlia e la stia proteggendo anche da *quello*, non solo dal mondo. Se non è voluto, va deciso quale versione tenere prima di scrivere altre card che la citano.

**Elemento critico #2 — inconsistenza minore di nome**
"Kaladin" compare come Nargathon (Alyssa.md), Ashwood (Dinastie), e senza cognome (Nixara.json) per lo stesso Direttore Sicurezza DCC. Andrebbe fissato un cognome canonico.

**Cosa aggiungerei alla card di Erik (materiale già presente in lore ma non nella card):**

- **Il Legame Caccia-confirmed.** La lore dice esplicitamente che Erik ha *sopravvissuto alla rottura di un Legame Caccia-confirmed* con Nixara — cosa definita "biologicamente straordinaria", visto che secondo le meccaniche LSE rompere un bond romantico "può causare malattia o morte". Questo spiega meccanicamente perché il suo trauma è così abnorme, non solo emotivamente ma biologicamente. Attualmente la card dice solo "shattered" — è molto più debole del vero lore.
- **Nixara come White Moon, Anointed da Wulfnic.** Non un dettaglio da poco: è la prima Anointing di un Living Saga in oltre tre secoli. Spiega perché Erik si inchina solo a Wulfnic — non è "suocero", è il religioso capo supremo che ha consacrato sua moglie.
- **Data matrimonio 1996** (oltre al bonding 1994) — manca del tutto.
- **Villa Douglas concreta**: indirizzo (555 Oak Road, Seven Hills), il Clan Seal (teschio di lupo runico che si illumina nelle notti di luna piena per comunicazione telepatica), nome ufficiale del suo den ("Erik Sanctuary"), squadra PMC nominata. Attualmente la card resta generica ("sprawling mansion").
- **Ciclo di Rut di Erik** — mai menzionato. Il system_prompt cita "prime Alpha Command, scent communication" ma non il Rut mensile (3-10 giorni) né la capacità di un Alpha di scentare la gravidanza di un'Omega dal collo — meccanica LSE canonica che potrebbe emergere in scene con Omega presenti nel pack.
- **Blocco extensions.wyvern** — la card di Nixara ha `chat_name`, `display_description`, `profile_bio`, `content_rating`, `visibility`; quella di Erik no. Vale la pena allinearla per coerenza di piattaforma e per la scheda che Wyvern mostra in preview.
- **Tag di rating** — la card ha contenuti espliciti nel lorebook (Intimacy Profile) ma nessun tag "Mature"/NSFW dichiarato.

Vuoi che integri tutto questo nella card (tenendo la questione Alyssa come nota a parte finché non decidi), o preferisci prima chiarire il punto #1 sull'umanità/natura di {{user}}?

content.thinking:
Lord Cornelius Douglas founded House Douglas in 1666, and the lore suggests a continuous lineage down to Erik, born in 1969. That means Magnus Douglas III, as Erik's father, must fit somewhere in that chain between the founder and Erik.

Given werewolf longevity — Pureblood Houses reaching 200-400 years — Magnus at 85 lands squarely in the "Elder" life stage (60-100+), described as an advisor and wisdom-keeper with reduced fertility and high social respect, which matches his retirement to a private wing and his aristocratic bearing. That aristocratic manner despite being born in America is explained by him being sent to study in England, tying back to House Douglas's English colonial roots in the Pacific Northwest.

This tracks well: Magnus is devoted to commerce like the family's founding legacy, likely preceding Erik as the patriarch before DCC expanded internationally, and he's notably secular — respecting Wulfnic as a powerful figure but rejecting any religious authority, which sets up a nice generational contrast with Erik's near-reverent deference to the Faith of Fenris.

For Elizabeth Duskwood, I'm thinking through establishing House Duskwood as a new Pureblood House with its own distinct physical traits — something like dark auburn hair and silver eyes — to differentiate it from Douglas and Bloodmoon coloring, while flagging this as new canon I should confirm.

I also need to figure out where these two fit in the world's tiered NPC system (party, active pool, remaining pool, background). Since Magnus and Elizabeth seem like static side characters tied to a reserved wing rather than core companions, they're probably best suited to the background or remaining pool tier.

The user's phrase "tra gli NPC" for the paternal grandfather is ambiguous — it could mean a full standalone Wyvern character card like Erik's, or just a lorebook/NPC entry referenced within existing family lore. I should ask for clarification on which approach they want before proceeding.

Actually, given the guidance to favor proceeding over asking, I'll just do both: create a compact background-tier NPC card for Magnus plus one for Elizabeth, and update Erik's family/connections section to mention his parents at the villa. That covers either intent efficiently — starting with a minimal House Duskwood color trait definition, then building Magnus's card as a JED+ background character.

Given the effort level calls for conciseness, I'll aim for compact profiles rather than full mega-JSON cards, flagging the invented details like House Duskwood traits and Elizabeth's secondary sex before finalizing anything. I think the best approach is proposing both NPC profiles in compact prose form first, then asking whether they want standalone JSON cards or just the lore integrated into Erik's book.

Actually, I'll be decisive instead and produce both a concise write-up and generate the JSON files directly, matching the pattern established in this conversation, while clearly flagging what's invented so they can correct me. Since there's no existing lore about House Duskwood's naming or color traits, I'll invent ash-grey silver hair and storm-grey eyes to match the twilight-themed name, positioning them as a Pureblood house.

I'll place them geographically near Blackwood as a rival or allied house, keeping details brief given the moderate effort level, and produce compact profiles plus two JSON files rather than exhaustive blocks. I'm working out ages — Magnus at 85 and Elizabeth at 76 both qualify as Elders — but since Purebloods live 200-400 years, I want to note Magnus is a "young elder" who wouldn't look or act frail by human standards, and I need to figure out their birth years from there.

Setting the current year around 2024 puts Magnus's birth around 1939 and Elizabeth's around 1948, which lines up with Erik being born in 1969 when Magnus would have been about 30 — that checks out. Now I'm sketching Magnus Douglas III's profile: Werewolf, Pureblood, House Douglas, likely Alpha given the patriarchal succession pattern of the house, though I'm considering whether he held Pack Leader status before Erik took over rather than being Beta or Delta.

Given his commerce-focused, secular, aristocratic personality that doesn't lean into Wulfnic reverence, being Alpha doesn't strictly require him to have been a warrior-leader — since Alpha status and pack leadership aren't the same thing per canon, he could fit better as a statesman or merchant type who never needed to lead in battle. I'll settle on Alpha for him to preserve continuity with the house's black hair and amber eyes trait line and to make sense of Erik also being an Alpha, even though secondary sex isn't strictly hereditary.

At 85, an Elder now with silver-white hair (aged from black) but retained amber eyes, he carries an English aristocratic bearing from an Oxbridge-style education, having built the original Douglas trading and shipping empire that Erik later transformed into the DCC. He's profoundly secular, skeptical of the Faith of Fenris, and while he respects Wulfnic as a powerful political entity, he rejects his religious "Living Saga" status.

This creates friction with Erik, who's grown quasi-religious in his deference to Wulfnic since Nixara's death. Magnus lives in a reserved, private wing of Villa Douglas, and his relationship with Erik reflects a classic old-money reserved patriarch clashing with a new-money, emotional, therapy-speak son -- he finds Erik's "therapy speak" distinctly American and a bit embarrassing to his English sensibilities, though he worries for him underneath it all.

Now I'm turning to Elizabeth Duskwood-Douglas -- a 76-year-old Pureblood Werewolf of House Duskwood, an Omega. She's an elegant, refined matriarch archetype, likely a warm grandmother figure who contrasts with Magnus's more reserved character.…

Ottima aggiunta — dà a Erik un contraltare familiare (nonno secolare/commerciante vs nipote quasi-religioso verso Wulfnic dopo Nixara). Ho controllato: nessun conflitto con la lore esistente, e si aggancia bene alla fondazione di House Douglas (Lord Cornelius Douglas, 1666, governatore coloniale inglese) — spiega perfettamente perché Magnus, pur nato in America, abbia modi aristocratici inglesi.

Un paio di scelte che ho dovuto inventare (dimmi se vuoi cambiarle):
- **Magnus**: Alpha, Pureblood House Douglas (coerente con la linea patriarcale)
- **House Duskwood** (nuova, per Elizabeth): non ancora canonizzata da nessuna parte — propongo capelli grigio cenere e occhi grigio tempesta come tratto di Casata, in stile "dusk/crepuscolo"
